Select the option which has nearly the same meaning as the underlined phrase.Despite presenting well-documented evidence and expert testimonials, the scientist's theory about time perception being altered by emotional intensity was met with provoking disbelief by many in the academic community. Although the hypothesis challenged conventional understanding, it opened new avenues for research into the intersection of psychology and physics.

Comprehension:Read the given passage and answer the questions that follow. In 1895, Birsa, a man from the Munda tribal group in Chottanagpur, Jharkhand, was believed to have miraculous powers to cure diseases and multiply grain. Declaring that God appointed him to save his people from trouble and free them from the slavery of dikus (outsiders), Birsa gained thousands of followers who saw him as bhagwan (God). His followers included other tribal groups like the Santhals and Oraons. They were unhappy with the changes and problems under the British rule, fearing for their livelihoods, religion and familiar ways of life.Why did thousands of people follow Birsa?
options: People believed that he was God incarnate and could solve their problems.
People believed that he would give them wealth and money.
People believed that he threatened them.
People believed that he was a thief and had loads of cash.
questions.explanation: सही उत्तर विकल्प 'A' (People believed that he was God incarnate and could solve their problems.) है।
